subject.title: feat(durable): hand off wakes to session queue

question: Should a durable wake queued as a `systemEvent` survive a reset or session-generation change, and which of this PR or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107559 should be the canonical landing branch?
rationale: The current queue intentionally lets `systemEvent` entries cross generation changes, while `agentTurn` continuations are generation-fenced; source and proof establish the mechanics but cannot decide whether durable wake attention belongs to the session key or a specific session generation.

options.title: Use refreshed canonical PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107559, port the existing live proof to its exact head, and explicitly document and test generation-agnostic wake attention.

options.title: Fence wakes to generation
options.body: Add an expected session-generation identifier and skip or supersede the wake after reset before selecting the canonical PR.

options.title: Retain this PR
options.body: Rebase and sequence this proven branch as canonical, then close the newer duplicate only after confirming it contains no unique work.

recommendation.title: Use refreshed canonical PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107559, port the existing live proof to its exact head, and explicitly document and test generation-agnostic wake attention.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work established the queue’s distinction between generation-fenced `agentTurn` continuations and generation-agnostic `systemEvent` delivery.
